question: The ‘Our Children Cultural Space’ (ECuNHi – Espacio Cultural Nuestros Hijos), set up by the Mothers of Plaza de Mayo association in Buenos Aires, is an important space dedicated to remembrance, culture, education and the promotion of human rights in Argentina.

For decades, ECuNHi has helped to preserve the memory of the victims of the military dictatorship and to run cultural and civic activities open to society as a whole. However, following the ideological budget cuts imposed by the Argentinian far-right government, which particularly affect human rights organisations, ECuNHi is currently facing serious financial difficulties.

The situation is exacerbated by the worrying condition of the building, which requires urgent infrastructure work to ensure users remain safe and its work can carry on. In view of this, can the Commission say whether EU financial instruments, particular in the fields of culture, historical memory, civil society and fundamental rights, can be accessed by an organisation like ECuNHi?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.10.2026) The EU attaches great importance to the promotion and protection of human rights which constitutes a core component of the EU’s external engagement.

The Commission also supports civil society organisations worldwide through its thematic programmes on human rights and democracy and civil society organisations, including actions promoting fundamental rights, civic space and culture.

The EU Delegation to Argentina publishes regular calls for proposals under the thematic programmes of fthe Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument – Global Europe (NDICI–Global Europe).

Under NDICI–Global Europe, the thematic programme on civil society organisations aims to promote an inclusive, participatory, empowered and independent civil society and democratic space in partner countries, while fostering inclusive and open dialogue with and among civil society organisations. In Argentina, these objectives are supported through regular calls for proposals published by the EU Delegation.

In addition, the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values programme1 supports organisations active on fundamental rights and EU values. The programme is open to all eligible organisations established in Member States, as well as in those third countries which have concluded an association agreement with the EU for participation in that programme. This is not the case for Argentina.
